title: Orchestrator-Centered Multi-Agent Systems for Clinical Reasoning
text:
This project develops a multi-agent clinical reasoning system in which specialized large language model agents generate, review, and refine diagnostic predictions through structured multi-step interactions.
The central orchestrator learns how to select agents, assign roles, and determine when to stop. The project investigates reinforcement learning methods based on diagnostic performance and inference cost, with the goal of supporting systems aligned with clinical decision-support workflows.

title: Sequential Anomaly Detection with Local and Global Explanations (GLEAD)
text: GLEAD is a globally and locally explainable method for sequential anomaly detection. It uses multi-head self-attention and prototypes for normal and abnormal sequences, providing local explanations by highlighting anomalous entries and global explanations by identifying common anomaly patterns across data.

title: Sequential Anomaly Detection with Local and Global Explanations (GLEAD)

title: Achieving Counterfactual Explanation for Sequence Anomaly Detection (CFDet)
text: CFDet is a counterfactual explanation framework for one-class sequence anomaly detection models such as Deep SVDD and OC4Seq. It identifies anomalous entries by determining the minimum changes needed to make a sequence normal, supporting security analysis and reducing false alarms.

title: BadSAD: Clean-Label Backdoor Attacks against Deep Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection
text:
BadSAD is a clean-label backdoor attack against Deep Semi-Supervised Anomaly Detection (DeepSAD) models. It combines trigger injection in normal images with latent-space poisoning so that triggered anomalies are misclassified as normal.



Published in the 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2025).

title: He Cheng
text:
About me
He Cheng, Ph.D., is a Postdoctoral Researcher in the Department of Biomedical Informatics at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. His current research focuses on scalable retrieval over large biomedical knowledge graphs and reinforcement learning for multi-agent clinical reasoning.
His previous research focused on interpretable and robust anomaly detection, including local, global, counterfactual, and prototype-based explanations, as well as backdoor attacks against anomaly detection models. He earned a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Utah State University, an M.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the State University of New York at Binghamton, and a B.E. in Mechanical Engineering from China University of Petroleum (East China).

title: He Cheng
text:
My research
I develop scalable methods for multi-hop retrieval over large biomedical knowledge graphs and integrate retrieved evidence with large language models for clinical applications. I also develop orchestrator-centered multi-agent systems, using reinforcement learning for agent selection, role assignment, and stopping decisions.
My earlier work includes counterfactual explanations (CFDet), local and global explanations (GLEAD), prototype-based explanations, and backdoor attack frameworks (BLOG, BA-OCAD, and BadSAD) for anomaly detection.

title: Backdoor Attack Against One-Class Sequential Anomaly Detection Models (BA-OCAD)
text: BA-OCAD is a backdoor attack framework for one-class sequential anomaly detection models such as Deep SVDD and OC4Seq. It uses trigger generation and backdoor injection to allow anomalies to evade detection while maintaining benign performance.

text: BA-OCAD is a backdoor attack framework for one-class sequential anomaly detection models such as Deep SVDD and OC4Seq. It uses trigger generation and backdoor injection to allow anomalies to evade detection while maintaining benign performance.

title: Backdoor Attack against Log Anomaly Detection Models (BLOG)
text: BLOG is a backdoor attack framework for self-supervised log anomaly detection models such as DeepLog and LogBERT. It combines data poisoning using normal log entries with a modified training objective, allowing abnormal logs to evade detection while maintaining benign performance.

title: Backdoor Attack against Log Anomaly Detection Models (BLOG)
text: BLOG is a backdoor attack framework for self-supervised log anomaly detection models such as DeepLog and LogBERT. It combines data poisoning using normal log entries with a modified training objective, allowing abnormal logs to evade detection while maintaining benign performance.

title: Explainable Sequential Anomaly Detection via Prototypes (EASD)
text: This project develops a prototype-based framework for explainable sequential anomaly detection. Multiple prototypes represent different normal and abnormal sequence patterns, while contrastive learning and k-means clustering support instance-based explanations.

title: Explainable Sequential Anomaly Detection via Prototypes (EASD)

title: LogosKG: Scalable and Interpretable Knowledge Graph Retrieval
text:
LogosKG provides efficient, scalable, and interpretable multi-hop retrieval over large knowledge graphs. It uses matrix-based representations and GPU acceleration to support biomedical knowledge graphs at billion-edge scale.
The project integrates knowledge graph retrieval with large language models to support evidence-grounded responses and improve reliability in biomedical applications such as clinical diagnosis verification and decision support.



Published at the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2026).
